claimChanges.claimText: Khalifa University Library's Academic AI Tools guide establishes Responsible AI Use principles requiring researchers and students to keep critical judgment in the loop, verify claims and references against inaccurate or fabricated information, check course, university, journal, and funder rules, protect data before uploading personal or unpublished material, acknowledge AI use, and noting that tool inclusion does not mean approval for every academic context.
Khalifa University's 2024-25 Student Handbook states that academic dishonesty in any form undermines the foundations of higher education and will not be tolerated by the university.

Khalifa University Library's Medical AI Research Guide warns that ChatGPT can fail on article identifiers and citations, and says tools such as RefWorks or EndNote are still needed for collecting, managing, and formatting citations.

In its Medical AI Research Guide, Khalifa University Library identifies keyword generation, organizing search syntax, and translating Arabic research questions into English search terms as examples where AI can support medical literature searching, while noting limits in advanced database syntax.

Khalifa University Library's Medical AI Research Guide says AI can help with medical research but advises users to document the exact AI questions, answers, platform, and timing when using AI to help searches.

Khalifa University Library's AI tools guide lists several institutionally available or subscribed AI research tools, including LeapSpace, Primo AI Assistant, Scopus AI, ScienceDirect AI, EBSCO Research AI, and AL Manhal Arabic Platform AI.

Khalifa University Library maintains an Academic AI Tools guide that highlights tools supporting academic work such as discovering scholarly literature, organizing sources, drafting academic writing, and exploring emerging AI platforms, while aligning with library resources and best practices.
